examBlueprint.tests: Interpreting scientific text; passage drawn from B10.1 (the homeostasis passage)

standards.title: Homeostasis and feedback
standards.description: Students explain how the body maintains a stable internal environment.
iCan: I can define homeostasis as a stable internal environment despite external change, and name a regulated variable (temperature, blood glucose, pH)
I can describe the feedback loop: a stimulus, a sensor, a control center, and an effector that produces a response
I can explain negative feedback (the response reverses the change toward a set point) with an example, such as sweating or shivering
I can distinguish negative from positive feedback (which amplifies the change), and explain the levels of organization from cells to systems

exam.examItems: MC Q1, Q2; SA 11; Part 3 CER; Part 4 Diagram

standards.title: The nervous system
standards.description: Students explain how neurons carry and pass signals.
iCan: I can label a neuron (dendrites receive, cell body, axon carries, axon terminals) and state that it carries electrical signals fast
I can explain that the resting potential is maintained by the sodium-potassium pump, and that a stimulus can trigger an action potential
I can describe the action potential as a rapid depolarization then repolarization that travels along the axon (all-or-none)
I can explain the synapse: the signal crosses to the next cell using a chemical neurotransmitter in the synaptic cleft

standards.title: Circulation and gas exchange
standards.description: Students explain how the body transports materials and exchanges gases.
iCan: I can describe the heart pumping blood through a double circulation (pulmonary and systemic) and name the chambers (atria, ventricles)
I can tell apart arteries (away from the heart), veins (back to the heart), and capillaries (exchange)
I can explain gas exchange: O2 diffuses from the alveoli into the blood and CO2 diffuses out, down their gradients
I can connect the system to cellular respiration: it delivers O2 and glucose and removes CO2

standards.title: Digestion and nutrition
standards.description: Students explain how food is broken down and absorbed.
iCan: I can tell apart mechanical digestion (physical breakdown) from chemical digestion (enzymes breaking polymers into monomers)
I can trace food through the tract: mouth, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, and name a key step at each
I can explain that the small intestine is where most digestion and absorption occur, aided by villi that increase surface area
I can connect the absorbed monomers back to the macromolecules of Unit 2 and to fuel for respiration

standards.title: The immune system
standards.description: Students explain how the body defends itself.
iCan: I can tell apart innate immunity (fast, general: barriers, phagocytes, inflammation) from adaptive immunity (slower, specific)
I can explain that adaptive immunity recognizes specific antigens; B cells make antibodies and T cells help and kill infected cells
I can explain immune memory: memory cells respond faster and stronger next time, which is the basis of vaccination
I can describe a vaccine as a safe exposure that builds memory without causing the disease
